tier_reason: benchmarks.md does show Spire 114,511.6 req/s vs HAProxy 2.7.3 85,406.0 and Envoy 1.22.8 48,040.4, but those rows are not a fair comparison. The compose files committed with these numbers (commit 0cac057, 2025-06-13) give the hey load generator 12 CPUs for the Spire and nginx runs and 4 CPUs for the HAProxy, Envoy, Traefik and Caddy runs. In the 2023 run (benchmarks.md at 42659e7), where hey had 4 CPUs for every proxy, Spire (then Silverwind) was slower than HAProxy, so the win comes from a crippled baseline harness and the entry drops to tier D under the crippled-baseline precedent.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Page (2025-06-13 run): Spire 114,512 req/s (avg 2.2 ms, p99 11.8 ms) vs HAProxy 2.7.3 85,406 (1.34x, derived from page data), Envoy 1.22.8 48,040 (2.38x, derived from page data), Traefik 2.9.8 59,487 (1.93x, derived from page data; this Traefik row is copied unchanged from the 2023 run) and Caddy 2.6.4 13,168 (8.70x, derived from page data). nginx 1.23.3 reached 148,677 req/s, so Spire is 0.77x of nginx (derived from page data). In the 2023 run, where hey had 4 CPUs for every proxy, Silverwind (Spire's old name) reached 66,370 req/s vs HAProxy 81,674 (0.81x, derived from page data) and Envoy 61,847 (1.07x, derived from page data).
corrections.workload: hey -n 100000 -c 250 GET through each reverse proxy to one echo-server backend under docker-compose, with the proxy and backend each limited to 4 CPUs and 8 GB. The hey container's limit differs between runs in the checked-in compose files: 12 CPUs for Spire and nginx, 4 CPUs for HAProxy, Envoy, Traefik and Caddy. The Traefik run used the jmalloc/echo-server backend; the others used ghcr.io/lsk569937453/echo-server:0.0.5. Each proxy had one run of about 1 s. Harness adapted from NickMRamirez/Proxy-Benchmarks; configs are in benchmarks/{spires,haproxy,envoy,nginx,traefik,caddy}/.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated for any side. All proxies ran as prebuilt Docker images: lsk569937453/spire:0.0.24 (jemalloc via JEMALLOC_SYS_WITH_MALLOC_CONF), haproxytech/haproxy-ubuntu:2.7.3, envoyproxy/envoy:v1.22.8, nginx:1.23.3, traefik:v2.9.8 and caddy:2.6.4. The README's source build is cargo build --release.
corrections.caveats: Crippled baseline harness. The compose files committed with the 2025 numbers give the hey load generator 12 CPUs for the Spire and nginx runs but 4 CPUs for the HAProxy, Envoy, Traefik and Caddy runs, while benchmarks.md says every service was limited to 4 cores. Only the two 12-CPU rows jumped between runs (Spire 66,370 to 114,512 req/s, nginx 42,388 to 148,677); HAProxy stayed at 81,674 to 85,406. In the 2023 equal-CPU run Spire (then Silverwind) was 0.81x HAProxy. The Traefik row is copied byte-for-byte from the 2023 run and used a different backend (jmalloc/echo-server). Configs differ: nginx is tuned (4 workers, upstream keepalive 100), HAProxy has a minimal config with no timeouts, and Envoy's concurrency is not set. Envoy also adds headers that the echo backend returns, so its response is 294 bytes vs Spire's 155. Even so, Spire is slower than nginx in its own table (114,512 vs 148,677 req/s; p99 11.8 ms vs 4.9 ms). Each proxy had one hey run of about 1 s on the same PC as the load generator, with old HAProxy and Envoy releases and unstated build flags. The checked-in Spire compose sets CONFIG_FILE_PATH to /temp/app_config.yaml but mounts the file at /tmp/app_config.yaml, and app_config.yaml uses an older schema than the README, so the published harness may not run as checked in. The README headline 'Exceptional Performance' is not backed by a like-for-like win over any C or C++ proxy.
corrections.why_faster: The README credits the Tokio async runtime and the Hyper HTTP library, with no analysis. The repo history points instead to the harness: the measured lead over HAProxy and Envoy appeared only when hey's CPU limit was raised from 4 to 12 for the Spire run and not for the baselines. This is a product-level comparison, not a language-level one.

notes: Downgrade C to D: crippled baseline harness. Per the checked-in compose files, the load generator had 12 CPUs for Spire and nginx but 4 for HAProxy, Envoy, Traefik and Caddy; under the 2023 equal 4-CPU harness Spire was 0.81x HAProxy. Shortcomings to record: not faster than nginx in its own table (0.77x); Traefik row reused from the 2023 run with a different backend; untuned HAProxy and Envoy configs vs tuned nginx; single ~1 s runs; flags unstated; the checked-in Spire compose has a /temp vs /tmp config path mismatch. Metadata checks out (Apache-2.0 in a file named 'licence', 459 stars, 28 forks, not a fork, last commit 2026-01-28, active); the project was renamed from Silverwind and is not already listed.
